memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"As the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and the voice of
God answered him." - Ex 19:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The trumpet grows louder, and in the middle of it, a conversation.

Moses spoke, and God answered him.

Sit with how remarkable that is. The mountain is on fire. The ground is shaking.
An entire nation is trembling at a distance. And a man is having a conversation
with God.

Notice the direction: Moses spoke first, and God answered. God does not only
issue declarations from the fire. He responds to what a person says to Him.

That is worth holding on to when God seems overwhelming and distant. The same God
who shakes mountains listens when a person speaks.

Later, this is precisely what Christ makes possible for everyone. "For there is
one God and one mediator between God and mankind, the man Christ Jesus" (1 Tim
2:5). Moses stood in that role temporarily and imperfectly. Jesus fills it
permanently.

And so Hebrews says we may "approach God's throne of grace with confidence"
(Heb 4:16). Not from a boundary line at the foot of a burning mountain, but
through the Son.

You speak, and God answers. That was extraordinary at Sinai. In Christ it is
your daily privilege.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you expect God to actually respond when you pray?
2. What would you say to God today if you truly believed He was listening?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You listen when I speak. Through Jesus I come to You with
confidence. Amen.
